fields.title: 2. T4 — Amazon Leo US Consumer Commercial Launch Regions and Pricing: Observation Results
fields.md:
| Item | October issue record | Confirmed this round | Source grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| Consumer pricing | Not announced | **Not announced** — the official site lists no pricing, launch regions or dates, only three terminals (Nano ≤100Mbps · Pro ≤400Mbps · Ultra ≤1Gbps↓/400Mbps↑) | ② [leo.amazon.com](https://leo.amazon.com/) accessed 2026-10-23 · [Wikipedia overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Leo) |
| Launch timing (company statements) | "Targeting launch within the year, date TBD" | No change — "initial service within 2026, expanding from northern and southern latitudes toward the equator" (no date). Already slipped once, from "mid-2026" in May to "this year" in July | ⑤ [Light Reading 10/12](https://lightreading.com/satellite/amazon-leo-still-tracking-for-2026-service-launch-as-satellite-production-ramps) · [Light Reading 07/06](https://www.lightreading.com/satellite/amazon-leo-inches-toward-service-launch) |
| Satellites | 396 (10/12) | No change — **396 launched (14 production-batch launches), 4 deorbited → about 392 in orbit** (formula: 396 − 4). **0 launches** since the final Atlas V mission on 7/2 | ④ [Wikipedia launch list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Amazon_Leo_launches) · ⑤ Light Reading 10/12 |
| Next launch | — | **Vulcan LV-01, targeted 2026-10-29, 40 satellites** — first Vulcan mission ("within weeks", 10/8 Badyal) | ④ same as above · ⑤ [Tokenpost 10/08](https://www.tokenpost.com/news/technology/28368) |
| Production | — | 1,000th satellite completed (10/8), "6 months for the first 27 → now 27 per week" | ⑤ Tokenpost 10/08 |
| FCC 50% milestone | "Missed the 1,616-satellite deadline (7/30)" | **Correction**: not a miss but a **waiver** — Space Bureau order DA 26-553 of 2026-06-05 conditionally waived the 7/30 half-deployment milestone. Conditions: satellites launched after 7/30 lose spectrum priority (restored upon reaching 50%); the final 3,232-satellite deadline of 2029-07-30 is unchanged (originally authorized 3,236 satellites, reduced to 3,232 by an orbit-modification authorization; many secondary reports still give 3,236) | ③ [FCC DA 26-553](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-26-553A1.pdf) (confirmed via ¶3 and ¶11 of the original .txt copy — when correcting the verifier discrepancy) · [Benton 06/08](https://www.benton.org/headlines/fcc-grants-kuipers-request-extend-or-waive-interim-milestone) |
| Enterprise customers | — | Beta operating: JetBlue · Delta (contracts), AT&T (enterprise customer connectivity) — consumer and government not yet launched | ⑤ Light Reading 07/06 |

**Verdict**: T4 has **not occurred**. Rule R5 ("Kuiper has not launched a US consumer plan by end-2027 → base +5, bearish −5") is judged at end-2027, so it remains pending. The competition timeline (October issue 1-7, "2027–2028 real threat") is unchanged — if anything, the three months without launches since July push the threat timing back (estimate). The October issue's competition table wording "missed the FCC 1,616-satellite deadline" **did not reflect the waiver order**, so it is corrected in the table above.

**Preparing the comparison baseline (a yardstick to use if T4 triggers)**: The October issue's T4 condition for changing the judgment is "20% or more cheaper than Starlink". We could not read the official Starlink US residential pricing page this round (page body not received); secondary reports give, as of 2026-08, **100Mbps $55 · 200Mbps $85 · Max $130/month, kit $349 or $0 + $10 per month** (estimate; varies by address, congestion surcharge separate) ([TechLoy](https://www.techloy.com/starlink-10-monthly-kit-fee-new-customers/), [SlashGear 2026-01](https://www.slashgear.com/2084684/cheapest-starlink-residential-plan-50-dollars)). Official confirmation is a task for the next round. For Amazon's side, there is only the statement of a terminal price "under $400", and monthly fee estimates split between $55–65 and $100–120, so **we adopt neither** ([findcheapbroadband](https://findcheapbroadband.com/blog/amazon-leo-costs/), [utilitiesformyhome](https://utilitiesformyhome.com/providers/amazon-leo/) — ungraded, for cross-checking).
